messages:
Maya (CS): Hi team — Acme Support reports duplicate partial generations and a double charge after a flaky network. Root request id: req_0a3f9, session token: sess_77. They say reconnecting causes a new generation instead of resuming. Any quick checks?

Acme Support: Repro steps we used: connect SSE -> start generate -> drop connection at ~1.2s -> reconnect with same session token and streamId. We got a second partial generation that continued from beginning instead of resumed. Billing shows two billed responses.

Liam (Eng Runtime): Likely two possibilities: 1) client re-sent a full request (no idempotency key) so backend treated as new run; 2) resume token mismatch so server couldn't map to prior KV cache. Do we have their request headers and the exact reconnect payload?

Maya (CS): Provided headers: Authorization, X-Session-Token: sess_77, no Idempotency-Key header. Reconnect payload includes stream_id and resume_token fields. They said resume_token looked unchanged.

Sophia (SRE): Can we see server side logs for req_0a3f9 around 2026-08-03 14:22 UTC? I want to confirm: (a) whether the reconnect hit the same runtime shard, (b) whether we dropped the KV cache entry due to eviction or restart.

Liam (Eng Runtime): Quick check: if resume_token is present but not recognized, we should return a 410/RESUME_EXPIRED code and *not* start a new generation automatically. If they got a new generation with 200 OK, client likely retried the original POST instead of a resume handshake.

Darren (Billing): From billing logs I see two charge events for account acme-001 within 30s of each other tied to the same customer request_id meta, but different server run_ids (run_91 and run_92). That matches duplicate completed generations. We should plan a refund if it's user-facing.

Maya (CS): Acme says their client library attempts an automatic reconnect and if it doesn't get a resume-ack quickly it re-issues the original call. They didn't set an idempotency key.

Liam (Eng Runtime): Actionable repro steps for engineering:
1) curl to start SSE generation (no idempotency-key):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer x" -H "X-Session-Token: sess_77" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","input":"short prompt","stream":true,"stream_id":"s1"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/sse
```
2) Kill connection after first chunk.
3) Reconnect with a resume handshake:
```
POST /v1/resume HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer x
X-Session-Token: sess_77
Content-Type: application/json

{"stream_id":"s1","resume_token":"<token-from-client>"}
```
4) Observe whether server returns resume-accepted vs starts a brand new run.

Liam (Eng Runtime): Short-term mitigation for CS to propose to customer: set Idempotency-Key for the original request and ensure the client treats a missing resume acknowledgement as a transient error (wait/backoff) rather than immediately re-issuing a full new request. Also enable a client-side dedupe: ignore duplicate completed outputs within N seconds for same stream_id.

Sophia (SRE): I've flagged the runtime cluster that served run_91 for a possible restart around the time window. If the runtime restarted, KV cache could have been lost which would explain resume failing and client retrying. We should add a more explicit resume failure status so clients don't trigger full replays.

Darren (Billing): I'll tentatively approve a one-time refund for acme-001 pending CS confirmation. If we find the platform behaved incorrectly (accepted resume incorrectly), escalate for full reimbursement and note bug in billing ledger.

Maya (CS): I'll coordinate with Acme: ask them to try with Idempotency-Key and attach their client logs. If they confirm repro with idempotency in place we escalate to eng-runtime with run logs.

Acme Support: Thanks — we'll try the idempotency header and report back with logs.

Liam (Eng Runtime): Follow-ups for eng: (A) make resume-failures explicit (distinct error code) and document common client patterns; (B) add a server-side heuristic to mark immediate duplicate runs within X seconds as likely-retries and soft-dedupe charges; (C) reproduce locally with forced runtime restart to validate behavior.

Maya (CS): Filing an internal bug and linking to this thread. Will update once customer tries idempotency key. :thumbsup:
